newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan trade surplus falls 26.8 pct in March.
newsitem.headline: Japan trade surplus falls 26.8 pct in March.

text.p: Japan's customs-cleared trade surplus slid 26.8 percent in March from a year earlier to 818.34 billion yen, the Finance Ministry said on Thursday.
The trade surplus with the United States, often a source of trade friction, rose 11.2 percent in March from a year earlier to 379.83 billion yen. The figures were not adjusted for seasonal factors.
At Thursday's exchange rate of around 125.80 yen to the dollar, the overall March surplus stood at $6.49 billion, while the surplus with the United States was $3.01 billion.
Economists said the drop in the overall surplus in March would be the last before the surplus begins rising sharply in April, May and June.

Data for the business year which ended in March showed that the overall surplus fell 29.6 percent from a year earlier to 6.42 trillion yen ($50.9 billion), while the surplus with the United States slid 2.2 percent to 3.76 trillion yen ($29.8 billion).

Economists had expected the March surplus to slip, partly due to a healthy surplus in the same period last year and partly because of higher imports feeding a manufacturing rush ahead of a rise in Japan's sales tax to five percent from three percent on April 1.
